title: The Echo of New Lagos Again
premise: Gideon Zhou has spent eleven years alone tending the Verdance, a terraformed garden built for colonists still in cryosleep, while the orbital relay that once connected New Lagos to Earth went silent. When the ship Meridian returns from a failed deep-space survey carrying its crew biologically reversed into childhood, Gideon learns the truth: the colony's power core is failing, and there is only enough energy to wake half the sleepers. The returning children hold the key—a memory-echo of the core's original design—but waking them means choosing which half of humanity gets a future. Gideon, who chose invisibility to survive his own past crimes as the colony's disgraced chief engineer, must finally stand accountable, sacrificing the garden he loves and broadcasting his confession to wake all ten thousand sleepers at reduced odds rather than play judge over who deserves to live.
about_author: Juniper Coldharbour is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent three years working on closed-loop life-support experiments in the Atacama Desert before turning to fiction. Their work explores loneliness, ecological grief, and the quiet heroism of maintenance workers in futures that forgot them.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Ledger
chapters.summary: Gideon Zhou records his 4,000th daily log: pruning the Verdance, checking cryo-vaults, rationing a decaying power grid. Through his POV we learn he came to New Lagos to disappear after an engineering scandal killed nine people on Mars. Emotional beat: tender melancholy—the garden thrives for people who may never come.

chapters.title: Signal in the Dust
chapters.summary: A distress ping hits Gideon's patched-together receiver: the Meridian, presumed lost twelve years ago, is entering orbit. He scrambles to prepare landing infrastructure no one has maintained since the exodus underground. POV shifts briefly to the ship's captain, now a seven-year-old girl named Ada. Beat: dread sharpening into desperate hope.

chapters.title: Children of the Long Dark
chapters.summary: The Meridian lands; forty crew members emerge as children, their bodies aged backward by cryo-stasis failure and an experimental reversal drug. Gideon recognizes Ada's eyes—she was his protégée before the fall. They remember everything but inhabit small bodies. Beat: uncanny grief and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Core Remembers
chapters.summary: Ada reveals the deep-space mission found a resonance pattern that could restart the failing geothermal core—but the data lives in the children's neural echoes, fragmented across forty minds. Meanwhile the vaults' power drops below safe thresholds. Beat: the first ticking clock; Gideon's guilt resurfaces as the children need an engineer he swore never to be again.

chapters.title: The Census of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Gideon audits the cryo-vaults and discovers the brutal arithmetic: full revival of all ten thousand requires more power than exists; half can be saved if the core restarts. The colony council's old contingency files surface—a pre-approved triage list ranking sleepers by 'utility.' Beat: moral vertigo; survival priced in human worth.

chapters.title: Confessions in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Ada confronts Gideon with what she learned in deep space: his Mars scandal was covered up by the same colonial authority that wrote the triage list—and abandoned New Lagos deliberately. The children vote to trust him anyway. Beat: betrayal and forgiveness entwined; Gideon begins reclaiming his name instead of hiding it.

chapters.title: Sabotage Below
chapters.summary: Descending into the dead city to reach the core, the group finds evidence someone else survived underground for years—and sabotaged the backup generators to force exactly this crisis. A feral, half-mad former security chief, Okafor, believes only the 'useful' should wake. Beat: the theme made flesh; justice outside the law turns violent.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ten Thousand Names
chapters.summary: Trapped by Okafor's lockdown of the vault control room, Gideon faces the choice the plot has built toward: use the triage list to save half cleanly, or attempt a reckless full-revival cascade using the children's resonance data at catastrophic risk. He refuses to be the judge. Beat: climax of conscience—he chooses everyone or no one.

chapters.title: Resonance
chapters.summary: Gideon broadcasts his full confession colony-wide as the cascade begins, offering himself for judgment while the children's memory-echo stabilizes the core. Okafor, hearing the truth of his own family on the triage list, stands down. Vaults open one by one; some fail, most do not. Beat: catharsis—power surrendered becomes the thing that saves them.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Living
chapters.summary: Weeks later, ten thousand groggy survivors walk the Verdance under repaired light. Gideon submits to a tribunal convened by the awakened—not exile, but accountability—and Ada, still a child, argues his sentence should be service. He tends the garden for people already born. Beat: quiet resolution; survival's price paid in honesty, not blood.
